verdicts.note: Speaks throughout as a woman/girl contrasting herself with boys; metadata correct.
Explicitly says 'Mixed school' with a 1:5 girl:boy ratio.
Quantity surveying / commercial management / construction maps to Civil & Building Engineering; quote weak but dept correct.
Father had a construction firm; clear family member involved in the industry.
Quote shows father's equality message, not explicit engineering encouragement; thin, downgrade to low.
Interested because the work is 'more than going onto site'; supports interesting-work draw.
Computing/technology/'more than building' supports appeal of variety.
Commercial bit as fallback 'if I don't do well in the engineering sector' maps to good degree even if not entering profession.
Quote shows she TOOK maths/economics (economics is not science), not that she was GOOD at maths and science; does not support being good at maths/science.
Clearly intends to go on placement with a company already arranged.
'I needed work experience... wanted to put them into practice' is the primary stated reason; strongly agree justified.
'kept learning these things but wanted to put them into practice' explicitly supports applying theory.
'help me understand where I'm going' is vague re 'what industry is really like'; thin, downgrade to low.
Quote about wanting ongoing employment with the company only loosely maps to placement-as-job-prospects reason; thin, downgrade to low.
She adds choosing dissertation more appropriately; dissertation = final-year project.
Chartership noted as company-selection factor rather than explicit placement-counts-toward-chartership reason; stays low.
'I wasn't looking at the salary really' explicitly supports money not a driver = disagree.
'wouldn't do anything different... same area' supports pleased with the choice.
'learnt knowing people... being patient with people' supports course develops interpersonal skills.
'made new friends... which is really good' supports satisfied with friends.
'my female tutor's not really been that good... isn't kind' clearly supports dissatisfied with personal tutor.
Course head 'very encouraging' supports satisfaction with lecturer support; stays low.
'arrange meetings and no-one comes... bad times of group work' supports dissatisfied.
'working in a consultancy... having my own consultancy' explicitly supports consultancy.
'put on projects in different areas... that's why I took up this course' supports travel being important.
'looking at career prospects' is broader than promotion specifically; thin mapping, stays low.
'give the girls more work to do' is boys offloading/freeloading, not students being competitive; does not support the competit construct.
